info.title: Core System API
info.description:
Enterprise Core System — the cross-cutting capabilities (identity, ledger, wallet, payment, notification, webhook) shared across every product. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer pk_<prefix>.<secret>` — see `GET /v1/whoami`. 

## Reading this document 

- Every request body attribute has a description and a realistic example. `required` is marked. - Every operation carries an `x-required-scopes` field listing the API key scopes the caller must hold. - The wildcard scope `*` covers every concrete scope — a key issued with `--scope="*"` is the whole Core for this tenant and passes every scope check. - Every monetary POST under `/v1/payments/*` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header (cached response on replay, `409` on conflict). 

## Outbound events (Core → caller) 

The Core emits events on two planes — register `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints` to subscribe, or supply `callback_url` on `POST /v1/payments` for a per-payment delivery: 

- `WebhookEvent` — envelope `{id, type, data}` POSTed to subscribed endpoints, signed HMAC-SHA256 (headers `X-Signature`, `X-Timestamp`, `X-Event-Id`, `X-Event-Type`). - `WebhookEventType` — the closed enum of event types the Core emits (`payment.status_changed`, `notification.delivered`, `notification.read`, `notification.failed`, `wallet.credited`, `wallet.debited`, the `subscription.*`, `invoice.*` and `usage.*` commerce events of ADR-0084). - `PaymentCallbackEvent` — the body POSTed to a per-payment `callback_url`. Same signature scheme, per-payment secret returned once in the initiation response. 

## Errors 

Every error response is `application/problem+json` (RFC 7807) with `{type, title, status, detail, correlation_id}`. 422 from a `FormRequest` adds an `errors: {field: [msg]}` map. Quote `correlation_id` when contacting support.

put.description:
The customer is declared by the project: `externalRef` is the
reference it knows the customer by, and the same reference always
lands on the same customer — the route is idempotent by
construction.

Answers `201` when the customer was created and `200` when it was
updated; the `ETag` header carries the new version. `If-Match`
carries the version the caller last read: when it no longer
matches, the write is refused with `412 version-conflict` rather
than silently overwriting the change.

Requires the `customers:write` scope. The email and the phone are
returned only to a caller also holding `customers:read`
(ADR-0070 §Sécurité).

Every call counted by `POST /v1/usage`, oldest first, in a stable
order: reading the whole journal while new usage is recorded neither
repeats nor skips a line recorded before you started. Pass
`next_cursor` back as `cursor` to read the next page, and `null`
when there is no more. `created_from` is inclusive and `created_to`
exclusive, on the instant the line was recorded.

Requires the `usage:read` scope.

created and linked by the platform administrator — ask for one for your project. A name

whose phone is not linked yet says so explicitly.

the same value on the same project returns the original notification without a second
send. Without it, every request is a new send. There is no `Idempotency-Key` header here.

CreatePlanRequest.description:
`POST /v1/plans` — ADR-0071 §5.

The plan is created `draft`: it enters the catalogue only once a
version is published (ADR-0071 §2).

code.description:
The stable identifier of the plan within the project. It
never changes, and no other plan of the project may carry
it. It is format-checked so it can never be injected into
a URL, a log or a cache key (ADR-0071 §1).

name.description: The name of the plan, as the project shows it.

description.description: What the plan includes, in the words of the project.
examples: Un utilisateur, un numéro de WhatsApp, un support par e-mail.

visibility.description:
`public` plans are the ones the project may sell; a
`private` plan is reserved to its own contracts.

sort_order.description: The order the plans are listed in — the lowest first.

CreatePlanRequest.title: CreatePlanRequest

CreatePlanVersionRequest.description:
`POST /v1/plans/{code}/versions` — ADR-0071 §5.

A version carries the **terms** of a plan. Once published, it is
frozen — the price displayed, the price billed and the price
contracted can never drift apart (ADR-0071 §2).

price_minor.description:
The price of the period, in **minor units** of the
currency — 500 for 5,00 XAF, never 5.0 (G5).

currency.description: The currency of the price, as its ISO-4217 code.

interval_unit.description: The unit the period is counted in.

interval_count.description:
How many units a period lasts — 1 for a monthly plan, 3
for a quarterly one.

trial_days.description:
How many days the contract may be used before its first
paid period begins.

grace_days.description:
How many days the service keeps running after the period
ends, before the contract is suspended.

grace_access.description:
Whether the service stays reachable during the grace
period — read-only when it does not.

features.description:
The named features of the version. The names are the
**project's** — the Core checks their format, never a
list of them (ADR-0071 §3). A feature is never a price.

CreatePlanVersionRequest.title: CreatePlanVersionRequest

CreateSubscriptionRequest.description:
`POST /v1/subscriptions` — ADR-0072 §7.

Signing a contract twice on a replayed request is a real harm, not a
duplicate row: the route carries the `idempotency` middleware (G7).

customer_ref.description:
The reference the project knows the customer by — the same
reference the customer was declared with.

plan_code.description:
The code of the plan the contract is signed on. The
contract then **freezes** the terms of the version that
was published at that moment (ADR-0071 §Conséquences).

trial_days.description:
How many days the contract may be used before its first
paid period begins. It overrides the trial of the plan
version when it is set.

start_at.description: When the contract starts. Defaults to now.

CreateSubscriptionRequest.title: CreateSubscriptionRequest

EraseCustomerRequest.description:
`POST /v1/customers/{externalRef}/erase` — ADR-0083 §3.

The erasure destroys the **identity** of the customer — the name and
the contact — and keeps the row: the invoices reference it.

reason.description:
Why the identity of the customer is destroyed. It is kept
in the audit trail of the erasure — it explains the
decision, it never carries personal data.

EraseCustomerRequest.title: EraseCustomerRequest

customer_ref.description: The customer, by the reference your project knows it by.

flow.description:
Where the customer lands: `manage` (the home of the portal,
default) or `pay_invoice` (straight to an invoice, which needs
`invoice_id`).

invoice_id.description: The invoice to open with the `pay_invoice` flow.

return_url.description:
Where the portal's "Retour" button sends the customer. It must
be one of the origins you allowed in `PUT /v1/portal/settings`,
otherwise the call is refused (422).

customer.description:
Optional: declare or refresh the customer in the same call, so
your project needs no separate "sync customers" job. Needs the
`customers:write` scope. Omitted fields keep their value.

plan_code.description:
Optional: subscribe the customer to this plan **if it has no
live contract on it yet** — so the call is safe on every login.
Needs the `subscriptions:write` scope.

trial_days.description: Free trial days when the subscription is created by this call.

PayInvoiceRequest.description:
`POST /v1/invoices/{invoiceId}/pay` — ADR-0073 §2, the online
collection of an invoice.

The amount is **not** in the request: what is due on the invoice is
what is collected (ADR-0094 §8). The caller says only how the payer
will pay.

channel.description:
The rail the payer will use — the canonical channel of
the `payment` module (ADR-0038 §1), never the provider's
own name.

customer_phone_number.description:
The payer's number — optional: the project's own customer
record carries it (ADR-0070 §1).

customer_name.description: The payer's name — optional, same rule.

customer_email.description: The payer's email — optional, same rule.

customer_lang.description:
The language of the payer's provider — optional, same
rule.

return_url.description:
Where the payer comes back after paying — optional,
browser-side only (the server-to-server channel of the
`payment` module is its own `callback_url`).

PayInvoiceRequest.title: PayInvoiceRequest

PaymentCallbackEvent.description: Body POSTed to a payment's `callback_url` at every status change — byte-for-byte the webhook envelope (ADR-0061). Signed with the per-payment `callback_secret` returned once at creation: `X-Signature` = hex HMAC-SHA256 of `X-Timestamp + "." + raw body`. Headers `X-Event-Id`, `X-Event-Type` too.

id.description: Unique event id — the same as the webhook plane would use. Deduplicate on it.

type.description: Always `payment.status_changed` on this plane.

payment_id.description: The payment id returned when you created it.

reference.description: Your own reference: the `Idempotency-Key` you sent when creating the payment.

status.description: Canonical payment status. Intermediate: `pending`, `processing`. Final: `succeeded`, `failed`, `expired`, `canceled`, `refunded`.

is_final.description: `true` once the outcome is settled: deliver the order on `succeeded`, offer a new attempt otherwise. `false` = keep waiting.

failure_reason.description: Why the payment did not succeed; `null` on success and on intermediate statuses.

occurred_at.description: When the Core recorded this status (UTC). Use it to ignore an older notification arriving after a newer one.

confirmed_amount.description: ADR-0077: amount the provider confirmed it collected, in minor units, on a settled payment. null when the source did not confirm an amount, and on any other status.

exception.description: ADR-0077: amount_mismatch or currency_mismatch when the provider confirmed something else than requested. The payment is settled but NOT allocated: no wallet is credited. null otherwise. Open enumeration: ignore values you do not know.

PaymentCallbackEvent.title: PaymentCallbackEvent

PaymentFlow.description: Discriminates between the two payment initiation flows exposed by aggregator-style providers. `Payin` is the synchronous, app-driven flow (used by mobile apps and server-to-server integrations that drive the customer through their own UX). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /payin`; CinetPay exposes it as `POST /v2/payment`; MTN exposes it as `POST /collection/.../requesttopay`.  `Paylink` is the hosted-link, redirect-driven flow (used by web apps that hand the customer off to a provider-hosted page). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /paylink`; CinetPay returns a `payment_url` alongside the same initiation call (the discriminator is implicit).  Providers that do not distinguish the two flows (e.g. CinetPay) treat `Payin` as the default and ignore the discriminator on the `InitiatePaymentCommand`.
PaymentFlow.title: PaymentFlow

party.description: Your own reference of the party whose wallet is debited.

amount.description:
The amount that left, an integer in the currency's smallest
unit.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the amount.

description.description: A label returned in the wallet's history.

external_reference.description:
The proof of the payout you made outside the Core (the mobile
money transaction id, a bank wire reference…).

metadata.description:
Any JSON object of yours (4 KB at most once encoded), opaque to
the Core.

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`. The `webhooks:write` scope
is enforced in the controller against the calling Project.

url.description:
The public URL the Core POSTs the signed payload to
when an event matches. Must be reachable from the
Core's outbound network — no localhost, no
RFC-1918 ranges, no link-local addresses. The
reason is that a registered endpoint is retried
automatically for hours, so an address that points
at an internal service today could become an
unintentional exfiltration channel tomorrow. HTTPS
is required in production; HTTP is accepted only
for local development.

events.description:
The list of event types the endpoint wants to
receive. At least one entry is required. Use the
wildcard `["*"]` to subscribe to every event the
Core emits — useful for development, but avoid in
production because new event types are added
silently to wildcard subscribers and may break a
receiver that expected a fixed schema.

items.description:
One event type per array element. The currently
supported values are listed in the enum of this
field in `/docs/api`.

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.title: RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest

phone_number.description:
The phone number of the WhatsApp device that will
display the pairing code, in international format
(E.164, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`). The Core forwards
this value to the channel provider as the device
identifier for the linking flow. It is not stored
by the Core — the provider is the source of truth
for the session.

overlap_hours.description:
Hours the previous secret keeps signing deliveries
(`X-Signature-Previous`), from 1 to 72.

display_name.description: The name shown at the top of the portal. @example "Mon Auto-École"

logo_url.description: An https URL of your logo (shown at most 40px high).

support_url.description: An https URL or a `mailto:` address for "Besoin d'aide ?".

allowed_return_urls.description:
The origins (and optional path prefixes) a `return_url` may
point to. Exact match on scheme, host and port.

allowed_asset_origins.description:
The https origins (`https://cdn.mon-site.cm`, no path) your
`logo_url` and `support_url` may point to. Empty or omitted
on a project that never set it = no external URL accepted;
omitted on a project that did = the list is kept.

allow_self_cancel.description: May a customer stop their contract at the end of the period?

allow_plan_change.description: May a customer subscribe and change plan alone?

payment_channels.description:
Optional. By default the portal offers every payment channel the
platform can route for your project (you configure no payment
provider). List channels here only to NARROW that offer, e.g.
`["mtn_momo"]`. Empty = no restriction.

direct_login_enabled.description:
Offer your customers a login by code on the portal page
`/portal/{project_id}/login` (off by default). The code is sent on
WhatsApp from `direct_login_session`, which is required to enable it.

direct_login_session.description: The name of one of your WhatsApp sessions (the one you put in `variables.session`).

channel.description:
The channel the file will be sent through. See
`POST /v1/notifications/text` for the full
description; the rule is the same across all three
content types.

to_party_ref.description:
Opaque recipient reference in YOUR system. Same
semantics as `to_party_ref` on
`POST /v1/notifications/text`.

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the file. The
provider fetches it server-side and re-hosts it.
Must be reachable from the provider's outbound
network (no private IPs, no localhost) — same
constraint as `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`.
The provider downloads it itself, so it must be directly
downloadable without authentication or hotlink protection —
otherwise the send ends `failed`.

filename.description:
The filename the recipient sees and the
content-disposition header is built from. The file's
actual content is fetched from `media_url`.

mimetype.description:
The MIME type of the file
(`application/pdf`, `image/png`,
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`...).
Required because file extensions are not reliable
signals — the provider uses this to set
`Content-Type` when re-uploading.

caption.description:
Optional text rendered above the file in the
recipient's client (most chat platforms support a
short text + file combo). UTF-8. Provider length
limits apply.

variables.description:
Free-form map of provider-specific variables forwarded
as-is to the channel's adapter. See
`POST /v1/notifications/text` for the full contract.
For `whatsapp`, REQUIRED keys `phone_number` and `session`.

phone_number.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`, the WAHA adapter rejects
outbound messages without `variables.phone_number`.

session.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`: the name of the WhatsApp
session to send from — the number linked to it is the one
the message comes from. Sessions are created and linked by
the platform administrator (never by the client): ask for one
to be created for your project and use the name you were
given. A name that is not registered for your project (or
shared with all projects) is refused with a 422 and nothing
is sent. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters.

customer_ref.description:
The customer this message is billed to, by the reference you
declared it with (`PUT /v1/customers/{ref}`). Required only
when your project asked for every metered call to name its
customer; ignored when no meter is mapped to notifications.
A message beyond the customer's plan is refused with `429
quota-exceeded` and nothing is sent.

client_reference.description:
Optional opaque reference supplied by the caller.
Two requests with the same `client_reference` on the
same Project are deduplicated: the second one
returns the first one's notification, no second
send happens. Use this when you have your own retry
loop and want a safe re-play after a timeout. When
omitted, the Core generates a fresh UUID per request
and every send is treated as a fresh effect.

to_party_ref.description:
Opaque recipient reference in YOUR system. Same
semantics as `to_party_ref` on
`POST /v1/notifications/text` — the Core does not
resolve it; the provider adapter does, using
`variables.phone_number` and the channel's expected
addressing scheme.

media_url.description:
Publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL of the image. The
provider fetches it server-side and re-hosts it, so
you do not upload binary. The URL must be reachable
from the provider's outbound network (no private
IPs, no localhost) — this is the same constraint as
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`.
The provider downloads it itself, so it must be directly
downloadable without authentication or hotlink protection —
otherwise the send ends `failed`.

caption.description:
Optional text rendered alongside the image in the
recipient's client. UTF-8. Provider length limits
apply.

filename.description:
Optional filename hint the provider uses when the
image is forwarded as a file attachment.

mimetype.description:
Optional MIME type of the image. When omitted, the
provider infers it from the URL extension or the
upstream `Content-Type` header.

variables.description:
Free-form map of provider-specific variables forwarded
as-is to the channel's adapter. See
`POST /v1/notifications/text` for the full contract.
For `whatsapp`, REQUIRED keys `phone_number` and `session`.

phone_number.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`, the WAHA adapter rejects
outbound messages without `variables.phone_number`.

session.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`: the name of the WhatsApp
session to send from — the number linked to it is the one
the message comes from. Sessions are created and linked by
the platform administrator (never by the client): ask for one
to be created for your project and use the name you were
given. A name that is not registered for your project (or
shared with all projects) is refused with a 422 and nothing
is sent. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters.

customer_ref.description:
The customer this message is billed to, by the reference you
declared it with (`PUT /v1/customers/{ref}`). Required only
when your project asked for every metered call to name its
customer; ignored when no meter is mapped to notifications.
A message beyond the customer's plan is refused with `429
quota-exceeded` and nothing is sent.

client_reference.description:
Optional opaque reference supplied by the caller. Two
requests with the same `client_reference` on the same
Project are deduplicated: the second one returns the
first one's notification, no second send happens. Use
this when you have your own retry loop and want a
safe re-play after a timeout. When omitted, the Core
generates a fresh UUID per request and every send is
treated as a fresh effect.

channel.description:
The channel the message will be sent through. The Core
picks the right provider based on this value and the
calling Project's configuration. Adding a new channel
is a configuration change, never a code change —
check `/docs/api` for the current list.

to_party_ref.description:
An opaque reference that identifies the recipient in
YOUR system — a user id, an order id, a customer
record id. NOT a phone number and NOT an email
address: the Core does not know how to reach the
recipient from this value alone. How it gets mapped to
a real delivery address depends on the channel and
provider — typically by reading a field like
`variables.phone_number` you include below.

text.description:
The message body, UTF-8. Rendered verbatim by the
provider — the Core does not interpolate
`variables` into it. Provider-specific length limits
apply downstream (check the channel's adapter
documentation for the cap on the platform you target).
examples: Hello Marie, your order #1234 is confirmed.

variables.description:
Free-form map of channel-specific values. The keys
required depend on the channel: - `whatsapp`: REQUIRED keys `phone_number` (the recipient's
  international phone number, E.164, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX` —
  the example is a placeholder, use a number you own) and
  `session` (the WhatsApp session to send from, see
  below). A request missing either is rejected with a 422.

Any other key in this map is forwarded untouched.

phone_number.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`, the WAHA adapter rejects
outbound messages without `variables.phone_number`.
Validating here means a missing field produces a
clean 422 instead of an asynchronous cascade failure
the caller would only learn about by polling.

session.description:
When `channel = "whatsapp"`: the name of the WhatsApp
session to send from — the number linked to it is the one
the message comes from. Sessions are created and linked by
the platform administrator (never by the client): ask for one
to be created for your project and use the name you were
given. A name that is not registered for your project (or
shared with all projects) is refused with a 422 and nothing
is sent. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters.

customer_ref.description:
The customer this message is billed to, by the reference you
declared it with (`PUT /v1/customers/{ref}`). Required only
when your project asked for every metered call to name its
customer; ignored when no meter is mapped to notifications.
A message beyond the customer's plan is refused with `429
quota-exceeded` and nothing is sent.

client_reference.description:
Optional opaque reference supplied by the caller. Two
requests with the same `client_reference` on the same
Project are deduplicated: the second one returns the
first one's notification, no second send happens. Use
this when you have your own retry loop and want a
safe re-play after a timeout — the same key on a
re-play means "this is the same notification I tried
             * to send before, please don't double-send". When
omitted, the Core generates a fresh UUID per request
and every send is treated as a fresh effect (no
caller-side deduplication is offered).

status.description:
The outcome to simulate. All four are final: once applied,
the payment can no longer change.

reason.description:
Optional failure reason, returned as `error_message` on the
payment and in the notification.

StartPaymentRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/payments`. The `payments:write` scope is enforced
in the controller against the calling Project — this class only
validates payload shape.

Two headers sit above this body and are documented separately by
Scramble: `Authorization` (Project API key) and `Idempotency-Key`
(required on every monetary mutation — replay the same key to get
the cached response without re-charging).

channel.description:
The channel the customer will pay through. The Core
routes the call to whichever payment provider is
configured for this channel on the calling Project —
the caller never names a provider directly.

amount.description:
The amount to charge, as an integer in the currency's
smallest unit — which depends on the currency: `XAF` has
no subunit, so `100` means 100 XAF; `USD`/`EUR` use cents,
so `100` means 1.00. Never a decimal number. The
conversion from a displayed amount is the caller's
responsibility.

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 three-letter code of the currency. The
provider configured for the chosen `channel` must
support it — otherwise the request fails with a
422 `unsupported-currency` error before reaching the
payment network.

reason.description:
A short label for the payment, shown to the customer on
the hosted page and forwarded to the provider as the
transaction description. Max 255 characters. Not echoed
back in the API response — keep your own copy if you
need it later.

customer_phone_number.description:
The customer's phone number in international format
(E.164, e.g. `+2376XXXXXXXX`). Forwarded to the
provider so USSD prompts and OTP codes reach the right
line on mobile-money channels. Optional — providers that
need it for their flow will reject the request if it's
missing.

customer_name.description:
The customer's display name. Optional. Forwarded to the
provider and rendered on the hosted payment page where
the provider supports it.

customer_email.description:
The customer's email. Optional. Forwarded to the
provider for receipt delivery where supported. Not
persisted by the Core — the Core never holds customer
PII; whatever the provider does with it is the
provider's responsibility.

customer_lang.description:
The language the customer's payment prompt/page is shown
in. Only `fr` or `en` are supported by the payment
provider — any other value (including regional tags like
`fr-CM`) is rejected with a 422. Optional — the provider
falls back to its default when missing.

anyOf.description:
How the payment starts. `payin` is the synchronous,
app-driven flow: the Core returns immediately with a
transaction reference and the caller drives the
customer through their own UX. `paylink` is the
hosted-link flow: the Core returns a URL and the caller
redirects the customer there. If omitted, the
provider default applies (typically `payin`).

return_url.description:
Where to send the customer's browser after they
complete (or cancel) the payment on the
provider-hosted page. Best-effort: this is
browser-side only and may never fire (closed tab,
disabled JS, captive portal). For a reliable
server-to-server signal, use `callback_url` instead. Must be an `https://` URL (audit de sécurité 2026-10-29 #18): the
provider redirects the customer's browser to it as is.

wallet_recipient_external_ref.description:
Optional. The external reference of the wallet to
credit automatically when this payment reaches a
successful terminal state. When present, the credit
happens in the same database transaction as the
payment confirmation — no separate API call needed,
no window for race conditions. When absent, the
payment is a pure collection: the money is held by the
Core but no wallet is credited. The value must match a
wallet owned by the calling Project; the request fails
with a 422 `wallet-project-mismatch` otherwise.

callback_url.description:
Where the Core POSTs the server-to-server notification
when the payment reaches a terminal state. This is the
reliable channel — use it to update your own order
state, release stock, send a confirmation email, etc.
The body is JSON and signed with HMAC-SHA256 (headers
`X-Signature`, `X-Timestamp`); the secret is returned
in the initiation response and never again, so store
it at registration time. Distinct from `return_url`:
this is server-to-server, `return_url` is browser-side.

StartPaymentRequest.title: StartPaymentRequest

TransferFundsRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/wallets/transfers` (ADR-0065). The `wallets:write`
scope is enforced in the controller; `Idempotency-Key` by the route's
`idempotency` middleware (G7).

currency.description:
The ISO 4217 code of every leg's amount. One transfer moves a
single currency.

legs.description:
Between 1 and 20 movements, applied together in one ledger
transaction: every leg lands, or none does.

from.description:
Your own reference of the party whose wallet is debited. It
must already hold a wallet in `currency` with enough
available funds.

to.description:
Your own reference of the party whose wallet is credited. Its
wallet is created on first credit.

amount.description:
The amount moved by this leg, an integer in the currency's
smallest unit (`XAF` has none: `45000` is 45,000 XAF).

to_party_type.description:
The type given to the destination party if it does not exist
yet (lowercase, underscores). Ignored for an existing party.

description.description: A label for this transfer, returned in each wallet's history.

metadata.description:
Any JSON object of yours (4 KB at most once encoded), opaque to
the Core and returned in each wallet's history.

TransferFundsRequest.title: TransferFundsRequest

UpsertCustomerRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/customers/{externalRef}` — ADR-0070 §2.

The customer is **declared by the project**: the reference the project
knows its customer by always lands on the same customer.

display_name.description:
The name the project shows for this customer. It is a
business name, not a personal one: the personal values are
the contact below. It carries no control character
(ADR-0070 §Sécurité) — a name is displayed, logged and
compared, and a hidden control character in it is a trap.

email.description:
The contact address of the customer. It is **personal
data**: it is encrypted at rest and never used as a
search key (ADR-0083 §2). The same address cannot be
declared twice for the same project.

phone.description:
The contact number of the customer, in E.164. It is
personal data too (ADR-0083 §2).

locale.description:
The locale of the customer, used to format the dates and
the amounts shown to them. Defaults to `fr`.

metadata.description:
Technical identifiers of the project about the customer
(a segment, a school, a tenant). **Never personal data**
(ADR-0070 §1): at most 16 keys and 4 KiB, the same
ceiling the database enforces.

UpsertCustomerRequest.title: UpsertCustomerRequest

VoidInvoiceRequest.description:
`POST /v1/invoices/{id}/void` — ADR-0073 §3, the cancellation of an
invoice that has not been paid.

reason.description:
The motive of the cancellation — mandatory: a cancellation
is an accounting act, and an accounting act leaves a trace.

VoidInvoiceRequest.title: VoidInvoiceRequest

previous_secret_expires_at.description:
ADR-0082 §5 — while a secret rotation's overlap lasts, deliveries
also carry `X-Signature-Previous`; null otherwise. Serialized as
is in the public API, hence the snake_case name.

WebhookEvent.description: Body POSTed to every endpoint registered via `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints` — and, identically, to a payment's `callback_url`. Headers: `X-Signature` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of `X-Timestamp + "." + raw body`, with your endpoint secret — or the payment's `callback_secret`), `X-Timestamp` (Unix seconds), `X-Event-Id`, `X-Event-Type`, `X-Delivery-Id`. Answer `2xx` within 10 s; deduplicate on `id`. The example shows `payment.status_changed`.

id.description: Unique event id. The same event is delivered again on retry or replay with the same id: deduplicate on it.

type.description: One of the values from the WebhookEventType enum. Decide whether to consume based on this.

payment_id.description: The payment id returned when you created it.

reference.description: Your own reference: the `Idempotency-Key` you sent when creating the payment.

status.description: Canonical payment status. Intermediate: `pending`, `processing`. Final: `succeeded`, `failed`, `expired`, `canceled`, `refunded`.

is_final.description: `true` once the outcome is settled: deliver the order on `succeeded`, offer a new attempt otherwise. `false` = keep waiting.

failure_reason.description: Why the payment did not succeed; `null` on success and on intermediate statuses.

exception.description: ADR-0077: amount_mismatch or currency_mismatch when the provider confirmed something else than requested. The payment is settled but NOT allocated: no wallet is credited. null otherwise. Open enumeration: ignore values you do not know.
